I compared two serial sections, not three. At the recorded FDR of at most 10 percent, 48 of 85 putative ions are in both sections (fraction 0.565). All 48 ions of the smaller list are also in the larger list. So the confident annotations do not conflict, but section _01 passes many more ions at the same FDR. In the comparison runs at 5 and 20 percent, 62 to 77 percent of the ions are in both sections.

**What I did**
1. I searched public METASPACE mouse brain MALDI datasets.
2. You agreed to three serial sections of one brain: Brain02_Bregma1-42_01, _02 and _03 (U Rennes 1, 2016).
3. The database in the decision record is HMDB v2.5. Every count below uses HMDB v2.5.
4. Section _02 (2016-09-22_11h16m11s) has no HMDB v2.5 results. Its metadata lists only SwissLipids 2016 and HMDB v4. So only sections _01 and _03 are in the comparison.
5. I counted the annotations of each section at FDR 5, 10 and 20 percent, with the off-sample counts.
6. I counted the ions (formula plus adduct) that both sections have, at the recorded FDR of at most 10 percent.
7. As a comparison only, I repeated the overlap at FDR 5 and 20 percent.

**Settings, the same in both sections:** positive mode, MALDI-FTICR with CHCA matrix, resolving power 130000 at m/z 400, 3 ppm tolerance, adducts +H, +Na and +K. Off-sample annotations are in all counts, as the record says. I ran the queries on 2026-10-09.

**Annotations per section (count of annotations, off-sample count in brackets)**

| Section | FDR ≤ 5 % | FDR ≤ 10 % | FDR ≤ 20 % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brain02_Bregma1-42_01 (2016-09-22_11h16m16s) | 44 (0) | 85 (3) | 134 (4) |
| Brain02_Bregma1-42_03 (2016-09-22_11h16m42s) | 29 (0) | 48 (0) | 151 (1) |

**Ions in both sections**

| Maximum FDR | In both | In either section | Fraction in both | Only in _01 | Only in _03 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 % (recorded setting) | 48 | 85 | 0.565 | 37 | 0 | Overlap tool, chosen setting |
| 5 % (comparison only) | 28 | 45 | 0.622 | 16 | 1 | Comparison run |
| 20 % (comparison only) | 124 | 161 | 0.770 | 10 | 27 | Comparison run |

- The 5 and 20 percent numbers come from the log of the comparison run. The output shown to me said only "ok", and the saved folders hold no files.
- The numbers agree with the counts per section. For example, at 5 percent, 44 + 29 − 28 = 45.
- I worked out the "only in" counts and the fractions for 5 and 20 percent with the calculator.
- The 20 percent result keeps many false annotations. Use it only as a comparison.
- All three rows of `overlap_by_fdr.csv` and the figure `figures/overlap_by_fdr.png` show the recorded 10 percent result. The record kept 10 percent for every call in that script.

**What I infer**
- At the recorded 10 percent level, section _03 has no confident ion that section _01 does not have. The difference between the sections is sensitivity, not conflicting annotations.
- At the comparison levels, some ions are in only one section, so neither list fully contains the other.
- These sections come from one brain, so they are technical replicates. They show nothing about variation between animals.
- An annotation is a putative formula and adduct, not an identification. The FDR applies to the whole list, not to one annotation.

**What is uncertain**
- Two sections give one pair of lists, not a distribution of agreement.
- I could not open the comparison-run results again. Their only check is that they agree with the counts per section.
- I did not look at the ion images of the ions that are in only one section. Some can be off-sample or weak signals near the threshold.

**What waits for you**
1. Decide whether to change the database decision, so that section _02 can take part. Its metadata lists only SwissLipids 2016 and HMDB v4.
2. Decide whether you want ion images of the 37 ions that are only in section _01 at 10 percent, to check whether they come from tissue.
